<!-- version: 2.47.0 -->
If you sync a calendar over CalDAV, this update may bring you appointments you never knew were missing. Yuvomi decided whether to fetch a calendar entry by the name its server had given the file - and quietly skipped anything not named the way most clients name it. Some servers name entries differently, in particular for anything created by an app that talks to them another way, so on the same calendar part of the appointments arrived and part did not. Nothing said so: the sync reported success and a plausible count. The names no longer decide anything, and the next sync brings the missing entries in. If something still fails to arrive, the server log now names the entry and the reason, so it can be reported instead of just being absent.

Deleting a repeating appointment that comes from a synced calendar now asks first. It always removed the whole series, and that part is right - Yuvomi cannot take a single date out of a series that belongs to another calendar, it would simply come back on the next sync. What it did not do was say so. Tapping one date in the month view and pressing delete made every date of that series disappear without a word. The question now names what is about to happen, and it says what is actually true for the appointment in front of you: a birthday entry comes back on the next sync unless you change the birthday itself, an appointment from a subscribed calendar cannot be removed at its source at all. Single appointments are unchanged - the undo message still catches those.

On a computer screen, the bar at the top of a module fits on one line again. Tasks, Contacts, Budget and Birthdays had pushed it onto two, as had the calendar in its week, day and agenda views, which cost a strip of the screen on every one of those pages. In the calendar it also depended on how many layers you had switched on - holidays, school holidays, birthdays - because those chips never gave up any room. They now shorten their labels before the bar breaks, without ever becoming harder to tap.

Nothing needs configuring and there is nothing to do after the update. There are no database changes in this version.

Full release notes are available at https://github.com/ulsklyc/yuvomi/releases/tag/v2.47.0
